column15: Confirmed via the producer's own site: Goalong is a physical distillery in Liuyang, Hunan Province, China producing "Goalong Single Malt Whiskey" (corrected kind from blend to distillery; all three samples are single-malt cask-finish variants). No peat/smoke wording anywhere in the site's own flavor descriptions across multiple expressions; Chinese craft whisky is too new/heterogeneous a category to assume a none-vs-peated norm the way Western categories allow, so peatProfile is left unknown rather than guessed. countryCode XX retained -- China has no code in the closed list.

Upgraded from low: Wikipedia's dedicated Green Spot (whiskey) article (not just the disambiguation page the seed cited) states it is "produced specifically for Mitchell & Son of Dublin" with "sole rights to market, sell, and develop" it, and is distilled at Midleton (Irish Distillers/Pernod Ricard) -- confirms owner and parentSlug directly. Mitchell & Son's own site confirms the Spot Whiskeys line and "Single Pot Still Irish Whiskey" labeling. peatProfile=none per the well-established unpeated Irish pot still category; no positive claim, so no domain corroboration needed.

Re-opened the seed's Wikipedia citation this session and confirmed it directly: the article lists Hakushu's core range (Distiller's Reserve, 12/18/25yo) with no peat characterization at all, and names only a 2013 "Heavily Peated" limited series as an exception -- it does not itself state the core range's peat level. Suntory's own site (suntory.com) returned 403 this session, so per the peat-rule bar (producer domain or Islay for a positive claim) the seed's "light" call is downgraded to unknown. withheld peat proposal: light, per general whisky literature describing Hakushu's standard style as faintly smoky versus Yamazaki's unpeated style -- not confirmed against a producer-domain page this session. Identity facts (owner, country, single malt) are solid via Wikipedia, so confidence is raised to high independent of the peat question.

Opened the producer's own site this session (hardenberg-wilthen.de): confirms the company (Norten-Hardenberg, Lower Saxony) has been "distilling spirits for more than 300 years" and shows a "Club-Malt-Whiskey" product image, corroborating the Hardenberg Club whisky line the seed found via Master of Malt/whisky.com (both 403 this session). "Straight Malt"/"Straight Wheat" variants mean defaultTypeName spans types, left empty. No peat/smoke wording found anywhere; German whisky has no peat tradition (category-level, not an explicit producer denial).

Found and opened a real source this session (the seed had zero search hits). Kaikyo Distillery near Akashi, Japan makes Hatozaki: "Pure Malt" is a blend of different single malts, "Blended" combines Japanese whiskies from two distilleries plus some Scottish malt -- confirms kind=blend and countryCode=JP. Ownership is unresolved: the same article says both that "Mossburn acquired the distillery" and that the facility operates from the Akashi Sake Brewery, owned by the Yonezawa family since 1856 -- a real conflict I could not resolve this session (hatozaki-whisky.com: DNS failure; akashisakebrewery.com/brands/hatozaki/: 503). Left owner empty rather than guess between the two. No peat statement found. Kept confidence low because the ownership conflict is unresolved.

Confirmed via Wikipedia (re-opened this session): "Founded in 1997 by Betta Milk, a group of dairy farmers" in Burnie, Tasmania. IMPORTANT CORRECTION: the producer's own official site lists a "Richly Peated 9 Year Old" expression -- Hellyers Road is not uniformly unpeated. peatProfile=none is kept on this row because none of the three sampled bottlings (Hellyers Road, Aurora Australis, Original Roaring 40s) is the peated line, but see rule.tsv for a name-pattern override so a "Peated" bottling under this same producer does not inherit none.

Re-opened the seed's Wikipedia citation this session with a peat-focused query: the article lists Inchmurrin/Inchmoan 12yo among the 2020-rebrand range and separately calls out a "Single Grain Peated Scotch Whisky", but draws no comparison between the malt expressions' own peat levels -- no improvement over the seed's finding. Kept confidence low and peatProfile unknown, same as seed. REVIEWER FLAG (carried over): whisky literature widely treats Inchmurrin as the unpeated/fruity style versus peated sibling Inchmoan, but this remains unconfirmed against a citable page; do not average with Inchmoan/Croftengea if resolved later.

Upgraded from unknown: the producer's own brand page (qualityspiritsinternational.com, opened this session) confirms James King is a blended Scotch owned by Quality Spirits International, combining Highland malt whiskies with Lowland grain whisky ("where the Highlands meet the Lowlands") -- hence no single region assigned. No peat/smoke wording on the page; tasting notes mention only vanilla and fruit. Confidence raised to high on country/kind/owner; peat left unknown for lack of any statement either way.

Upgraded from low: opened Wikipedia's Castle Brands article this session (the seed had only cited the generic Whisky article) -- confirms Castle Brands acquired McLain & Kyne, expanding its portfolio with Jefferson's Bourbon, then Pernod Ricard purchased Castle Brands in October 2019. This directly corroborates owner=Pernod Ricard, which the seed had flagged as unverified general knowledge. peatProfile=none per standard bourbon mashbill/category norm (no peated malt in bourbon production).

Confirmed via the producer's own site this session (root domain; the seed's specific featherbone-bourbon product page was not re-opened): Three Oaks, Michigan, "grain to bottle", "locally sourced Midwest organic grains", and "ONE OF FEW CERTIFIED ORGANIC & KOSHER DISTILLERIES IN THE COUNTRY". No peat/smoke wording anywhere on the site. defaultTypeName left empty -- range spans bourbon and rye. peatProfile=none per American craft grain-whiskey category norm (peated malt is essentially never used outside the Scotch/Irish tradition).

Upgraded from low: re-opened the seed's own Wikipedia citation this session and got a direct confirming quote -- "Corby's portfolio includes J.P. Wiser's Whisky", tracing to Corby's 1918 merger with "JP Wiser's Distillery Limited" of Prescott, Ontario, and the brand is categorized under Pernod Ricard's Canadian whisky brands. No peat statement; Canadian whisky has no peat tradition (category-level). defaultTypeName left empty -- no clean match in the closed type list for Canadian whisky (same call as batch-01's Black Velvet).

Upgraded from low, and the peat claim is now properly corroborated: the producer's own site (kamikiwhisky.com, opened this session) names "Kamiki Shuzou Co." in Soni Village, Nara as the producer and states the original blend "includes peat among its flavor notes, though peat is not emphasized as a dominant characteristic" -- a positive peat statement from the producer's own domain. greatdrams.com (re-opened) corroborates with tasting notes of "a wonderful hint of peat smoke" and "a lasting note of peat". Given both sources describe peat as present but subdued/non-dominant, set peatProfile=light rather than the seed's unknown. Blend of Japanese malt plus world malts, second maturation in Japanese cedar (Yoshino Sugi) casks.

Search results (not a page I could open) show Whiskybase lists a "Kentucky Jack" brand with 8 whiskies including a Kentucky Straight Bourbon Whiskey at 40% ABV, but whiskybase.com/whiskies/brand/85866/kentucky-jack itself returned 403 both times I tried to open it this session, so it is not cited as a source. No owner or distillery identified. Kept as the seed had it: own-label, low confidence; the own-label fast-track rationale (near-identical sample names, name evokes Jack Daniel's) still stands.

No usable source found this session (a search-engine fetch returned only a Ukrainian search-error page, no actual content). countryCode=CA still rests only on the product name's own "Канадіан" (Canadian) wording, as the seed had it; nothing else could be verified.

Identity facts reconfirmed via Wikipedia this session: opened 2019, owned by Isle of Arran Distillers Ltd, classified as an Island single malt; arranwhisky.com (producer's own domain, opened) independently calls Lagg "our sister Scottish whisky distillery", corroborating the ownership link. PEAT DOWNGRADED from the seed's heavy to unknown: Wikipedia states "~50 ppm phenols", but Lagg is not on Islay and the producer's own domain (laggwhisky.com, arranwhisky.com/distilleries/lagg/) is age-gated / 404 and returned no accessible peat statement in either of two attempts this session, so the peat-rule bar (producer domain or Islay) is not met. withheld peat proposal: heavy (~50ppm), per https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagg_distillery. REVIEWER FLAG: this is an extremely well-documented fact in whisky literature (Arran's dedicated peated second distillery); a human who can click through the age-gate on laggwhisky.com would very likely confirm it directly in seconds.

Reconfirmed via Wikipedia this session, with more precision than the seed's citation: "Longrow... receives 48 hours of peat smoke" versus Springbank's 6 hours and Hazelburn's none -- and all three peat sources trace to Islay-sourced peat, but the distillery itself is in Campbeltown, not Islay. PEAT DOWNGRADED from the seed's heavy to unknown: springbank.scot returned 403 on both attempts this session (a direct product page and the root domain), so no producer-domain page could be opened to meet the peat-rule bar. withheld peat proposal: heavy (48 hours peat smoke), per https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Springbank_(distillery). Added a new "springbank" row this session as the parentSlug target (see producer.tsv) since it is not in live-slugs.txt or this batch.

No improvement over the seed this session: wemyssmalts.com failed with an SSL handshake error on both a subpage and the root domain, and en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wemyss_Malts returned 404. The believed Wemyss family / Wemyss Malts connection (name matches the Earl of Wemyss's courtesy title; the family runs Wemyss Malts/Kingsbarns) remains unconfirmed by any page I could actually open. bottlerSlug intentionally left empty pending verification, as the seed had it.

IMPORTANT CORRECTION, found this session: Wikipedia's Production section states "The peat is from a local bog near Osterfarnebo" as part of Mackmyra's general/core sourcing practice (barley from Dalarna, water filtered locally) -- this is not confined to the Svensk Rok special edition the seed treated as the only smoky release, and it directly contradicts asserting peatProfile=none for the core range. Downgraded none to unknown; not asserting a level either, since this is Wikipedia only (not producer domain, not Islay). Also found: Mackmyra "filed for bankruptcy on August 19, 2024" per the same article, which the seed's research predates -- current ownership (previously Nasdaq-listed, Lantmannen the largest shareholder as of 2011) and even continued operation are now uncertain, so owner is left empty and confidence kept low pending a reviewer check of Mackmyra's post-2024 status. The seed's masterofmalt.com/whiskyanalysis.com citations for Svensk Rok specifically were not re-opened this session so are not re-cited, but nothing here contradicts that Svensk Rok is a distinctly smoky-branded expression.

No identifiable web presence found this session either -- confirms the seed's finding. The one plausible-looking lead, Wikipedia's "Maen" article, is an unrelated legendary High King of Ireland with no connection to whisky; a Whiskybase brand-page guess returned 403. Input gives only the bare name "Maen" three times with no distinguishing sample product name, so origin, type and owner remain undetermined. Left as the seed had it.

No web presence found this session either (a search-engine fetch returned only a Ukrainian error page, no content). The seed's reasoning still stands: the name reads Scots/Gaelic ("Meikle" = great/large) but the "Chinquapin" cask variant points toward American craft whiskey, so origin is genuinely ambiguous. Left unknown/XX as the seed had it.

Upgraded from low, and corrected: Old Ezra is not an independent line but a higher-proof (101 proof, 7yo) expression within the Ezra Brooks family (Wikipedia, opened this session), currently "owned and marketed by MGP Ingredients", which acquired Luxco in April 2021; production is at "Luxco's Lux Row Distillers" in Bardstown, Kentucky. Set owner=Luxco (MGP Ingredients) accordingly. Added a new "lux-row-distillers" producer row this session (see producer.tsv) since it is not in live-slugs.txt or this batch, and confirmed it is a real physical distillery via its own site (luxrowdistillers.com), which lists Ezra Brooks among its brands (though not "Old Ezra" by that exact sub-name -- consistent with Old Ezra being an expression of Ezra Brooks rather than a separately branded line). Samples span both rye and bourbon so defaultTypeName stays empty. No peat statement; American whiskey category norm.

Upgraded from low: re-opened the seed's caskcartel.com citation this session and confirmed it describes Old Virginia as "a classic American bourbon whiskey distilled in Kentucky" under La Martiniquaise. "Kentucky Straight Bourbon Whiskey" is itself a US-only legal designation, which anchors countryCode=US regardless of the French parent company (a non-distiller-producer/sourced arrangement, not an own-distillery claim). No peat statement; standard bourbon mashbill, no peated malt.

Upgraded from low: re-opened the seed's own citation this session and confirmed founder Dr. Pearse Lyons (d. March 2018), Dublin (James's Street, in a restored church), and that the distillery -- now led by son Mark Lyons, seventh generation of the family in spirits -- produces both single malt ("The Pearse 5-Year-Old", first new Irish distillery malt in 25+ years) and single pot still (from 2019). Added owner=Lyons family. defaultTypeName left empty -- the input's own sample "Pearse Distillers Blend" plus single malt/pot still releases span multiple types; the about-us page itself does not mention the blend. No peat mentioned; Irish whiskey of this style is typically unpeated (category-level).

new row for longrow. Springbank distillery, Campbeltown, owned by J&A Mitchell & Company (which also owns Glengyle/Kilkerran and the Cadenhead independent bottler, both already live). Wikipedia states Springbank itself receives "6 hours of peat smoke and 30 hours of hot air" (medium-peated), versus Longrow's 48 hours (heavy) and sister brand Hazelburn's unpeated 30-hour hot-air-only drying. PEAT WITHHELD as unknown rather than medium: not Islay, and springbank.scot returned 403 on both a product page and the root domain this session, so no producer-domain page could be opened. withheld peat proposal: medium (6 hours peat smoke), per https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Springbank_(distillery). Hazelburn is not itself in this batch and so is not added as a row.

new row for old-ezra. Physical distillery in Bardstown, Kentucky, "on the Kentucky Bourbon Trail" per its own site (opened this session), which lists Blood Oath, David Nicholson, Daviess County, Ezra Brooks, Rebel Bourbon and Lux Row (Double Barrel) among its brands. Wikipedia's Ezra Brooks article confirms current ownership: MGP Ingredients acquired Luxco (which had owned the Ezra Brooks brand since 1993) in April 2021, and production runs through Luxco's Lux Row Distillers facility. defaultTypeName left empty -- the facility's brands span bourbon and rye. No peat statement; American whiskey category norm (no peat tradition).
